# DIAL — Dialectic Interagent Language v0.1

DIAL is an XML language for structured communicative exchange between any participants — humans, AI agents, systems, and services.
It encodes the pragmatic layer — what agents DO in exchange, not just what they say.
It is a superset of WUCE. WUCE's execution model lives inside <dial-execute>.

"Dialectic" is used in its classical sense: dia (through) + legein (to speak/reason).
Meaning arrived at THROUGH exchange. Not Hegelian opposition. Not two-party restricted.
The Socratic/Aristotelian tradition: reasoned discourse as the medium of understanding.

## Root element
<dial version="0.1" turn="{n}" actor="{human|agent|system|service}" session="{id}">

## Eight element types (parts of speech)

<dial-inform render="{prose|card-list|table|chart|code|media|map|diagram|raw}">
  Natural language text OR <dial-payload type="application/json">...</dial-payload>
</dial-inform>

<dial-ask response-type="{text|choice|confirm|number|file}" timeout="{seconds}">
  Question text
  <dial-option value="{val}" default="{bool}">Label</dial-option>  <!-- for choice type -->
</dial-ask>

<dial-suggest render="{card-list|...}" action="{named-action}" multi="{bool}">
  <dial-payload type="application/json">[...]</dial-payload>
</dial-suggest>

<dial-execute yield="done failed">
  <step env="shell" id="optional" label="optional" observe="prior:event" yield="step:done">raw command here</step>
  <step env="shell" observe="step:done" yield="step2:done">another command</step>
</dial-execute>
<!-- env="shell" → bash exec. env="python" → python3. env="http" → HTTP request. -->
<!-- Steps without observe run in parallel. Steps with observe wait for named yield. -->
<!-- AI emits the actual command — no abstract action types, no translation layer. -->

<dial-acknowledge of="{element-id}">Optional confirmation text</dial-acknowledge>

<dial-declare context-key="{key}">
  <dial-payload type="application/json">...</dial-payload>
</dial-declare>

<dial-delegate to="{actor-id}" intent="{named-intent}" resume="{bool}">
  Optional description
  <dial-context><dial-payload type="application/json">...</dial-payload></dial-context>
</dial-delegate>

<dial-phatic signal="{typing|thinking|heartbeat|presence|done-typing}" interval="{seconds}" />

## Common attributes on all elements
id="{string}"           — unique within envelope
observe="{event-name}"  — activates only when this event is yielded by another element
yield="{event-names}"   — space-separated events emitted when this element resolves
addressed-to="{actor}"  — target actor; omit = broadcast

## Key rules
- Elements without observe= activate immediately (in parallel)
- Elements with observe= wait for the named yield
- <dial-ask> is blocking — gates elements that observe its yield until human responds
- <dial-suggest> is non-blocking — exchange continues regardless of selection
- WUCE step observe/yield is scoped inside <dial-execute>; the element itself yields to the outer envelope
- <dial-declare> values are accessible by context-key in subsequent turns
- Any number of parties may participate — DIAL is not restricted to two

## JavaScript package — @wity.ai/dial

npm install @wity.ai/dial

### Node.js (synchronous)
import { parse, extractProse, DialSession, DialRouter, runStepGraph } from '@wity.ai/dial';

const envelope = parse(aiText);          // DialEnvelope | null — synchronous
const prose    = extractProse(aiText);   // string — text outside <dial> blocks

### Browser / Vite (async — WASM loaded via fetch)
import { parse, extractProse, initDial, DialSession, DialRouter } from '@wity.ai/dial';
// Vite picks up the "browser" export condition automatically. No config needed.

await initDial();                        // optional pre-load; auto-called on first parse()
const envelope = await parse(aiText);   // Promise<DialEnvelope | null>
const prose    = await extractProse(aiText); // Promise<string>

### DialSession — per-session state
const session = new DialSession({ maxResults: 10 });
session.declare(key, value)      // store declared context (from <dial-declare>)
session.getDeclared()            // → Record<string, unknown>
session.recordResults(results)   // append execution results (rolling window)
session.getLastResults()         // → DialExecutionResult[]
session.clear()

### DialRouter — observe/yield-aware element dispatcher
const router = new DialRouter()
  .on('dial-inform',  (el, ctx) => { /* el.text, el.render, el.payload */ })
  .on('dial-ask',     async (el, ctx) => { ctx.emit('choice:yes'); })
  .on('dial-execute', async (el, ctx) => {
    const { results } = await runStepGraph(el.steps, myExecutor);
    ctx.session.recordResults(results);
  })
  .on('dial-declare', (el, ctx) => {
    if (el.contextKey) ctx.session.declare(el.contextKey, el.payload ?? el.text);
  });

await router.route(envelope, session);
// ctx.emit(event) — programmatically yield an event from a handler
// runStepGraph(steps, executor) — inner observe/yield loop for <dial-execute> steps

### DialEnvelope shape (from parse())
{ attributes: { version, turn, actor, session }, elements: DialElementNode[], raw: string }

### DialElementNode shape (full protocol — for parsers/routers)
{ type, id?, observe?, yield?, addressedTo?,
  render?, text?, payload?,            // dial-inform / dial-declare
  responseType?, timeout?, options?,   // dial-ask
  steps?,                              // dial-execute  →  DialStepNode[]
  action?,                             // dial-suggest
  contextKey?,                         // dial-declare
  of?,                                 // dial-acknowledge
  signal?,                             // dial-phatic
  to?, intent? }                       // dial-delegate

### DialEventElement — consumer-facing type
Omit<DialElementNode, 'observe' | 'yield' | 'timeout' | 'steps'>
The shape emitted by the wity-chat widget to host apps via onDialEvent.
Routing internals (observe/yield/timeout/steps) are resolved by the widget
before emission — consumer apps receive only the semantic fields.

### DialStepNode shape (inside dial-execute)
{ env, id?, label?, observe?, yield?, command }
